scope: Theorem 11.5 of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 44-45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For any machine and finitely specified initial tape, an effective smooth force on R3, periodic from time zero, with one compact spatial support and bounded mixed derivatives, realizes the event ∃t ≥ 0 : X(t; 0) ∈ (−6, −4) × (−1, 1) × (−1, 1) ⇐⇒ halting. 44 The zero-data velocity is unique among classical smooth solutions with bounded u, ∇u, u ∈ CH2 ∩ C1L2 and p ∈ CL2 on every finite interval. The prescribed solution has uniformly bounded kinetic energy.
